en: Vimānavatthu: The Mansion of the Man,
Chapter on Well-Placed [Offerings]
8. The Story of the Many-Colored Mansion Having ascended a mansion of many colors and manifold designs,
which dispels both fear and sorrow—
Surrounded by a host of celestial nymphs, you rejoice like Sunimmita, the lord of the bhūtas.
There is no one equal to you; how much less anyone superior?
Through his merit and through his supernormal power,
all the gods of the Thirty-three hosts gathered together and paid him homage,
just as the gods pay homage to the Moon.
And these nymphs all around you dance, sing, and delight you.
You have attained the divine power of a god, O one of great majesty.
"What merit did you perform while being a human being?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing majesty,
and why does your complexion illuminate all directions?"
Thus that son of the gods was delighted...
[as before] ...the fruit of which deed this is.
“Venerable sir, in the past I was a disciple of the Victor named Sumedha;
I was an ordinary person, lacking realization.”
Thus I shall wander as a mendicant for seven years.
I [shall serve] the Teacher, the Conqueror Sumedha,
who has attained final Nibbāna, crossed over the flood, and is a Tathāgata.
Having paid homage at the stupa, which was covered with a net of gold and filled with precious gems, I gladdened my mind.
I had no month’s worth of alms, nor was there anything for me to give.
But there, I indeed encouraged them:
"Worship this relic of one worthy of worship;
thus, it is said, you shall go from here to heaven."
That very same wholesome deed was performed by me,
and I myself experience divine happiness;
I rejoice in the midst of the hosts of the Thirty-three gods.
He did not reach the exhaustion of that merit.
Thus ends the eighth [chapter], the *Anekavaṇṇa-vimāna*.
